checks.sources_say: Customer email states 'Policy number: VER-1004' and the Policy Schedule in the claims system shows policy_id VER-1004 with holder Thomas Petit
checks.evidence: Customer email signature block; Policy Schedule (claims system)

checks.sources_say: Email describes damage to the policyholder's own car after hitting the car in front in a traffic jam — a collision damaging the insured vehicle, which is coverage C2 'Collision damage' (contract Article 2); C2 is listed in the Policy Schedule coverages
checks.evidence: Customer email body; Veridia contract Article 2 coverage table (document 2630#10414, page 1-2); Policy Schedule coverages [C1, C2]

checks.sources_say: Email: 'an accident that happened on 08 October 2026'
Email received on 2026-10-10 (header date), reporting the 2026-10-08 accident — 2 calendar days later, within the 5-day deadline of contract Article 4.1
checks.evidence: Customer email header 'received on 2026-10-10'; Veridia contract Article 4.1 (document 2630#10414, page 2)

checks.sources_say: Email: 'The garage quoted €1,500 to repair my car.' Contract Article 1 defines repair cost as the total incl. VAT on the quote; the attached repair_quote.pdf is stored by the mailroom and cannot be opened, so the quote's total-incl.-VAT line cannot be verified directly, but no source contradicts €1,500
checks.evidence: Customer email body; Veridia contract Article 1 definition of repair cost (document 2630#10414, page 1); repair_quote.pdf listed as received by the mailroom but not openable

checks.sources_say: Email: 'I hit the car in front of me in a traffic jam. My fault.'
Email: 'I hit the car in front of me' — another vehicle and its driver (Mr. Blanc) were involved
Email names the other driver: 'Mr. Blanc and I signed the accident report'

Email lists attachments damage_photos.zip, repair_quote.pdf, accident_report_signed.pdf; the mailroom confirms the same three files were received. These are exactly the three documents required for C2 under contract Article 4.3 (photos of the damage; repair quote; accident report signed by both drivers when a third party is involved). The files are stored by the mailroom and cannot be opened, so their belonging to policyholder Thomas Petit / vehicle VW Golf cannot be verified inside the files, but no source contradicts it
checks.evidence: Customer email attachment list; mailroom receipt note; Veridia contract Article 4.3 required-documents table for C2 (document 2630#10414, page 2)

checks.sources_say: No exclusion under contract Article 3 is stated anywhere: no alcohol/drugs, licence is valid (licence date 2008-11-01), no racing/track use, the damage was not intentional ('My fault' means at-fault, not deliberate), and it is collision damage, not wear/mechanical failure
checks.evidence: Customer email body; Veridia contract Article 3 exclusions list (document 2630#10414, page 2); Policy Schedule licence_date

verdict.summary: All recorded facts match the customer email and the Veridia contract (document 2630#10414): reported within the 5-day deadline, C2 collision coverage is in the Policy Schedule, all required documents were provided, no exclusion applies, and the playbook's commercial-vehicle referral rule is not triggered since the other vehicle is a private car, so the staged €1,200 payout (€1,500 repair cost minus €300 deductible, no assessor needed) should be approved.
